subject: Action plan & commit schedule for Veridian evaluation + region/residency pricing
messages:
From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Action plan & commit schedule for Veridian evaluation + region/residency pricing

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) to align the evaluation milestones, procurement checkpoints, and the commercial levers we discussed (commits, ramp, discounts, and region premiums). High-level summary below: 

- Week 0–3 (POC): deployment in us-west + limited multi-AZ failover testing. Redwood provides staging credits for 100k tokens and a trial model footprint.
- Week 4–8 (Eval): full ingest of test prompts, latency/residency verification. If Veridian requires data to remain in-region, we’ll enable the US-west residency pool (premium applies).
- Post-eval (close window): two-tier commit options: 6mo commit (mid) and 12mo commit (preferred) with step-up ramp at 3 months. Discounts scale with committed throughput and upfront payment.

Key asks for procurement to move fast:
1) Confirm residency requirement (in-region only vs. multi-region with encrypted cross-region failover).
2) Target close date (we proposed 2026-06-18 in the attached MAP so procurement can align).
3) Which commit band is more realistic for you (100M tokens/mo or 300M tokens/mo)?

I've attached the Veridian_MAP_v2.xlsx and a short residency pricing appendix that shows the premium bands (+10% / +18%) and cross-region failover terms. If you want, I can draft an SOW and DocuSign that mirrors the MAP milestones so legal/procurement can review quickly.

Would you be available Thursday 05/29 for a 30-min procurement + security touchpoint?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Business Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Veridian_MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), residency-pricing-appendix.pdf (pdf), SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf (pdf)

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@veridianhealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian Health - Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action plan & commit schedule for Veridian evaluation + region/residency pricing

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. Quick clarifying questions from our side before we lock the touchpoint:

1) Residency: For PHI workflows we need in-region processing and at-rest residency; cross-region failover is allowed only for the control plane and encrypted KV fallback — customer data must not be served out of-region except via encrypted, policy-controlled failover. Can you confirm Redwood's technical constraints here and whether the residency premium in the appendix covers that?

2) Pricing: The premium bands look reasonable but we need a worked example showing true run-rate at 3 and 12 months for both commit bands with a best-, likely-, worst-case usage profile.

3) SLA/rollback: If we see regressions in latency when failing over cross-region, is there a contractual rollback or credit?

Procurement is available 05/29 1400 PT — we can take the 30-minute slot.

Thanks,
Emily Carter
Head of ML Platforms, Veridian Health
emily.carter@veridianhealth.com

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Action plan & commit schedule for Veridian evaluation + region/residency pricing

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in. Emily confirmed procurement touchpoint tomorrow at 14:00 PT and asked three specific follow-ups (residency technical assurance, run-rate worked examples, and SLA/rollback language). Can you: 

- Marissa: produce 3-month and 12-month run-rate examples for the two commit bands (100M/mo and 300M/mo) with best/likely/worst usage. Include token cost, residency premium, and the resulting blended $/1k tokens.
- Karthik: confirm technical constraints for PHI-in-region processing and whether our failover mode (control-plane vs. data-plane) matches Emily's requirement. Also advise recommended contractual credit language if failover causes latency regressions.

Soojin — FYI; if legal has standard rollback credits for cross-region failovers, please flag. We want to keep the procurement call focused.

I'll draft an SOW skeleton after we have the numbers.

Thanks,
Rafael

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Action plan & commit schedule for Veridian evaluation + region/residency pricing

Rafael / Karthik — attached are the worked examples (I pasted a short summary here):

- 100M tokens/mo commit band:
  - Best: 80M actual -> effective price $0.85/1k tokens (after 6% volume discount)
  - Likely: 110M -> effective price $0.72/1k (includes +10% residency premium)
  - Worst: 160M -> step-up pricing to $0.68/1k after ramp clause at month 3

- 300M tokens/mo commit band (preferred):
  - Best: 250M -> effective price $0.62/1k (10% upfront discount applied)
  - Likely: 320M -> effective price $0.55/1k (includes +18% multi-region residency premium in hybrid config)
  - Worst: 420M -> effective price $0.49/1k with overage scaling and capped overage at 1.5x baseline

Residency premium notes: in-region only deployments add +10% to base unit. Multi-region active-active with encrypted cross-region failover (data-plane allowed under DR conditions) is +18%. Appendix defines failover triggers (regional outage > 3m or sustained latency > 2x SLO for 5 consecutive mins).

I also included a sample credit schedule: 10% service credit for SLA misses during an enforced cross-region failover window, subject to remediation steps. Legal should confirm.

Happy to walk through the spreadsheets on the call.

—Marissa
Senior Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Action plan & commit schedule for Veridian evaluation + region/residency pricing

Quick tech confirmation:

- We can support PHI workflows with full in-region data-plane processing (us-west) and a control-plane that communicates across regions. We will not shard customer plaintext across regions unless an encrypted failover is triggered.
- Cross-region failover modes:
  - Control-plane failover (orchestration only): no premium.
  - Encrypted data-plane failover (driven by DR playbook): allowed, but requires HSM-backed key wrapping and the +18% premium for multi-region data availability.

SLA/rollback recommendation: include a clause that gives Veridian the right to revert to single-region routing and receive a pro-rated credit if post-failover latency regressions exceed SLO by >25% for more than 10 minutes after remediation attempts. Suggested credit: 5–10% depending on duration. Legal to finalize exact wording.

We'll also add a short checklist for the eval run (latency probes, residency verification test cases, crypto audit steps).

—Karthik
Director, Inference Platform

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@veridianhealth.com>, Veridian Health - Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action plan & commit schedule for Veridian evaluation + region/residency pricing

Hi Emily — thanks for the quick questions and for booking the call. I summarized answers below so procurement has the numbers ahead of the 14:00 PT touchpoint: 

1) Residency: We can run PHI data fully in-region (us-west) for the eval. Our encrypted data-plane failover option (DR) is available and carries the +18% premium; control-plane failover is orchestration-only and does not move customer data across regions.

2) Run-rate worked examples: attached (see "Veridian_MAP_v2.xlsx") — Marissa included best/likely/worst and the blended $/1k tokens factoring residency.

3) SLA & rollback: Karthik suggested a credit schedule (5–10% pro-rated credit) if latency regressions post-failover breach SLOs per the remediation timeline. We will have legal draft the exact contract language; for procurement call we can agree to the principles.

Next steps I propose after the call:
- We finalize the MAP milestone dates and lock a target close of 2026-06-18.
- I’ll push a DocuSign-ready SOW that mirrors the MAP (link below) so procurement/legal can begin review in parallel.

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.example.com/servlet/documentsigning?env=prod&doc=VDH_MAP_v2

See you on the call.

Best,
Rafael

Attachments referenced: Veridian_MAP_v2.xlsx, residency-pricing-appendix.pdf, SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf
